headline_marked: Trump says [[replacing FIFA's Infantino would be a 'terrible mistake']]
headline: Trump says replacing FIFA's Infantino would be a 'terrible mistake'
summary: US President Donald Trump backed the FIFA leader amid allegations of a workplace affair and a failed private investment scheme.
details: US President Donald Trump has publicly backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino, describing him as "fantastic" in a Truth Social post.
Trump stated that FIFA would be making a "terrible mistake" if they considered replacing the Italian-Swiss lawyer.
The US President praised Infantino for presiding over the most successful World Cup ever, claiming it was four times more successful than previous ones.
Infantino is currently facing scrutiny over allegations of a workplace affair and criticism regarding a failed private investment scheme.
While Trump supports him, US Soccer, Canada Soccer, and football organizations in Central America and the Caribbean have issued statements critiquing the FIFA leader.
Other major bodies, including the Confederation of African Football and CONMEBOL, share Trump's position in supporting Infantino.
Infantino has denied all allegations of wrongdoing and is scheduled to face reelection next March.
FIFA has defended its president, calling the backlash a concerted effort by some to undermine the organization.
caption:
Donald Trump calls replacing FIFA President Gianni Infantino a "terrible mistake."

US President Donald Trump has publicly backed FIFA president Gianni Infantino, describing him as "fantastic" in a Truth Social post.

Trump stated that FIFA would be making a "terrible mistake" if they considered replacing the Italian-Swiss lawyer.

The US President praised Infantino for presiding over the most successful World Cup ever, claiming it was four times more successful than previous ones.

Infantino is currently facing scrutiny over allegations of a workplace affair and criticism regarding a failed private investment scheme.

While Trump supports him, US Soccer, Canada Soccer, and football organizations in Central America and the Caribbean have issued statements critiquing the FIFA leader.

Other major bodies, including the Confederation of African Football and CONMEBOL, share Trump's position in supporting Infantino.

Infantino has denied all allegations of wrongdoing and is scheduled to face reelection next March.

FIFA has defended its president, calling the backlash a concerted effort by some to undermine the organization.

headline: 132 killed as 7.4 magnitude earthquake hits Colombia
summary: The quake is described as the most powerful to strike the country in the 21st century, with heavy casualties reported in Pereira.
details: A powerful 7.4 magnitude earthquake has struck western Colombia, leaving at least 132 people dead. Rescue operations are currently underway to find those still missing beneath the rubble.
caption:
132 dead and counting. A 7.4 magnitude earthquake has devastated western Colombia.
